method: Both the retiring scraper and the new Core adapter were replayed offline against this SAME sealed capture, so the parity below is byte-level. This is the parity the inventory asked for before migrating this source.

transport_contract.pagination: AJAX /scroll/searchhash/{hash}/page/{n} with X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest; the hash comes from the first page

declared_budget.why: The ceiling is 26 pages. The scope DECLARES four — the initial listing plus three scroll pages, the 83 offers measured live, about twice what the producer's dynamic budget fetches. Widening it is a params decision with its own validation, not a code change.

live_state.note: Only HALF the detail pages carry a JSON-LD JobPosting (41 of 83), so a detail without it is the normal case and the listing stub stands on its own: title, company, city and canton all come from the listing.

deliberate_improvements.what: a multi-valued employmentType is rendered instead of lost
deliberate_improvements.effect: the producer carried the list straight into a string column; Core renders 'FULL_TIME, TEMPORARY'

deliberate_improvements.what: identity is the portal's own job id (J991993)
deliberate_improvements.effect: a retitled offer keeps one identity, and a tracking query is the same offer

preserved_quirks: data-nextpage and the fragment's nextpage are cast safely: int('') used to take the whole sweep down and lose the details already downloaded.
A failure mid-scroll is REPORTED: learning only the first page would leave the scroll pages unfetched forever.
A scroll response that is not a JSON object, or carries no html, ends the sweep cleanly.
The listing metadata is read as 'CANTON · City · Company', and only a two-letter head counts as a canton.
An empty logo is not a logo.
notes: No credential exists for this source and none was created.
The artifact carries no personal data: only byte counts, hashes and counters.
